From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Retention routing & temporary BYOK exception — ops + compliance check-in

Team —

Helix Health asked for a short-lived BYOK/ephemeral retention carveout for their POC: 30-day log retention for session-level audit data (instead of our standard 90 days) and an ability to route audit exports to their escrow (they're using a managed HSM). They need evidence for an upcoming internal review next Friday.

As this touches product routing, KMS/BYOK handling, and compliance evidence, can we align on a minimal-safe path that meets the POC timeline? Specific asks from Helix are:
- Proof of per-request audit log capture (who/when/route)
- Confirmation of KMS key rotation policy if we allow their external key in the flow
- A short-term retention exception (30d) and a plan to revert to standard 90d after POC

Requests:
1) Ben — what evidence artifacts can we produce in 72 hours (logs, signed attestations, sample audit export)?
2) Marissa — engineering constraints for routing audit exports to an external escrow (format, delivery, encryption) and estimated effort for a temporary pipeline.
3) Jonas/Kim — any legal or SLA flags if we enable an external HSM handshake for a sandboxed tenant?

I'm scheduling a 30m bridge call tomorrow (Nov 16) to walk the group and confirm action items — but wanted initial notes here so we have an audit trail.

Thanks,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, security@helixhealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention routing & temporary BYOK exception — ops + compliance check-in

Thanks Grace — quick replies inline.

What we can deliver in ~72 hours (from now):
- Sample audit export: JSON lines with per-request metadata (request_id, model_id, timestamp, routing_decision, user_id obfuscated).
- Signed sample export: small PKCS7 envelope with our signing cert so Helix can verify receipt provenance.
- Short report: list of retained fields and redaction status (PHI-sensitive fields redacted per our policy).

Open questions / blockers:
- If we allow their external HSM to be used for encryption-at-rest of the export, we need a defined handshake and trust boundary. We can support wrapping/exporting to a customer-provided public key, but we cannot import or operate on their private key. That means customer-side key usage for server-side encryption must be explicit.
- Audit indexing: our current export schema includes the KV-cache keys for tracing (hashed). Are they expecting raw KV values? We should not provide raw cache contents.

Attachments: [attachment: audit_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet) — contains fields Helix asked for mapped to current export schema]

Proposed quick path:
1) Produce a sample signed export and schema mapping within 48–72 hours.
2) Enable a short-lived routing rule that duplicates audit events for Helix to a secure S3 folder encrypted with their pubkey (readonly).
3) Restrict retention to 30 days via a tenant-level policy flag; auto-revert after POC end date.

I'll bring a short checklist to the bridge call.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Security Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, security@helixhealth.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention routing & temporary BYOK exception — ops + compliance check-in

Adding engineering constraints:

Feasible short-term options (ordered by implementation speed):
A) Export duplication: duplicate audit events to an external S3 endpoint they control. We can deliver signed JSONL as Ben proposed. Estimated effort: 2 engineer-days + ops window to enable tenant routing. No model-serving changes.
B) Envelope encryption with customer public key: we can wrap exports with their public key client-side and write to their escrow. Effort: 3–4 engineer-days including key verification handshake. We will not accept or store their private key.
C) Live KMS integration (their HSM as a key provider for our tenant): Not feasible for POC — requires broader security review and changes to our KMS abstraction (4–6 weeks).

Retention toggle: we can add a tenant flag to set export retention to 30 days. It can be temporary and automatically removed on a configured date. Implementation: 1 engineer-day for the toggle + 0.5 for automated revert.

Operational caveat: duplicating high-volume audit streams creates egress cost and must be throttled. Propose a sampling policy if volume > X req/sec.

I'll prepare a minimal runbook and a diagram (proposed-byo-flow-diagram.png) before the call.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Principal Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention routing & temporary BYOK exception — ops + compliance check-in

Appreciate the clarity. A few product/program-level asks:

- Timeline: Helix needs evidence by next Friday (2026-11-26). That gives ~10 working days. With Ben/Marissa estimates this seems doable if we prioritize.
- Risk control: we should ship option A (export duplication + signed JSONL) as the immediate deliverable and gate B/C for later.
- Canary and rollback: require a canary tenant flag and a monitoring alert if export failure rate > 0.5% within first 24 hours.

Kim — can legal sign off on the temporary retention flag and the egress to their escrow with a short addendum? If procurement needs a template, we should offer a simple MSA addendum.

I'll mark this as high-priority in the sprint and allocate an engineer pair for two days to produce a sample.

-Jonas

Thanks — a few compliance notes before we proceed to dev:

1) Evidence package: Helix will accept the signed JSONL export plus an accompanying attestation document that lists the exported fields and redaction logic. Ben, please include redaction rules and the signing cert chain.
2) KMS/Key handling: we can allow export encryption with their public key (option B) as long as we document key-handling responsibilities in an addendum and run a short security questionnaire. We must not import customer private keys.
3) Retention exception: legal is okay with a timeboxed 30-day exception *if* we capture the decision in an internal approval ticket and present the mutual action plan to procurement.

Action items for Helix: provide the public key (PEM) for export wrapping, and confirm the S3 endpoint + IAM role or presigned URL pattern.

Let's make the bridge call this afternoon; I'll have a short template addendum for procurement to review.

Kimberly Park
